This involves transforming agriculture through conservation, mechanization, smart agriculture
and digitization, aligning with the UN’s Transitions of food systems and digital connectivity. The focus on marginalized groups, including

equity and social justice. The programs support human rights, incorporate humanitarian endeavours, and foster resilience and long-term
development in line with larger UN objectives. This will be achieved though coordinated effort with other regional frameworks, including the African Union’s Agenda 2063 for impactful outcomes.

projects.name: Strengthen HWC management by upgrading data systems, training staff, equipping regional units, and implementing mitigation measures, including predator-proof kraals and elephant-friendly water points. projects.description:

Deploy satellite collars and GPS transmitters on selected predators to enhance monitoring and research. Contract HWC research organizations to conduct a cost-benefit analysis of alternative mitigation measures, ensuring evidence-based interventions.

projects.name: Emergency response to enhance resilience and mitigate climate-induced impacts on livelihoods, food and nutrition security of the most vulnerable households in Namibia
projects.description: Contribute to improved evidence generation, and food security and livelihood diversification of El-Nino affected farming households - As more than 43% of the population was reported to be food insecure, Government availed NAD 829 million (USD 46 million) for the drought relief support program, leaving a funding gap of approximately NAD 482 million (USD 26 million). More than 70% of the drought relief support program is earmarked for food assistance. In light of the funding gap, and as expressed by OPM, there is an urgent need to avail fodder (hydroponic) for core breeding herds as well as small scale irrigation systems and vegetable seeds, and to support diversification of livelihoods through provision of low-maintenance livestock such as chickens and rabbits. Through this assistance, FAO Namibia aims to reach 1200 households (4,800 people) in Erongo, Hardap, Kunene, Omaheke and Otjozondjupa regions to improve livelihoods through enhanced agricultural production while contributing to strengthened capacity for resilience building.
